subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Where in the mitochondrion are the electron carriers of the electron transport chain located?
options: The inner membrane (cristae)
The matrix
The intermembrane space
The outer membrane
questions.explain: The chain of carriers is embedded in the folded inner mitochondrial membrane, the cristae.

questions.q: Besides reduced NAD, what TWO products result from the link reaction per pyruvate molecule?
options: Oxaloacetate and water
Glycerate-3-phosphate and oxygen
Lactate and ATP
Acetyl coenzyme A and carbon dioxide
questions.explain: Each pyruvate is decarboxylated and combined with coenzyme A to form acetyl CoA, releasing CO2 and reducing NAD.

questions.q: The induced-fit model differs from the lock-and-key model in that:
options: the active site changes shape as the substrate binds to fit more closely
the active site is exactly complementary to the substrate before binding
the substrate changes shape to fit a rigid active site
no enzyme-substrate complex is formed
questions.explain: In the induced-fit model the active site moulds around the substrate on binding, straining bonds and stabilising the transition state.

questions.q: Above the optimum temperature, enzyme activity falls because:
options: hydrogen and ionic bonds break, changing the tertiary structure and active site shape
more enzyme-substrate complexes form than can be processed
the activation energy decreases too far
substrate molecules move too slowly to collide
questions.explain: Excessive thermal energy breaks bonds holding the tertiary structure, denaturing the active site so the substrate no longer fits.

questions.q: What is the NET yield of ATP from one molecule of glucose during glycolysis alone?
options: 4 ATP
2 ATP
1 ATP
38 ATP
questions.explain: Four ATP are produced but two are invested in the early phosphorylation steps, giving a net gain of two ATP.

the rate of reaction at zero substrate
the substrate concentration at which the enzyme denatures
the optimum temperature for the enzyme
questions.explain: Vmax is the theoretical maximum rate achieved when enzyme active sites are fully saturated and working at capacity.

questions.q: A red blood cell placed in pure water bursts (haemolysis) because:
options: water leaves the cell by osmosis
water enters down a water potential gradient and the cell has no rigid wall to resist swelling
the membrane actively pumps water in
solutes enter the cell by active transport
questions.explain: Pure water has a higher water potential than the cytoplasm, so water enters by osmosis; lacking a cell wall, the animal cell swells and lyses.

questions.q: The fluid-mosaic model describes the cell membrane as:
options: a continuous protein sheet with no lipid
a single layer of phospholipids
a fluid phospholipid bilayer with proteins embedded in a mosaic pattern
a rigid layer of protein sandwiched between lipid
questions.explain: The model depicts a fluid bilayer in which proteins are scattered like a mosaic and can move laterally within the membrane.

questions.q: In aerobic respiration, what is the terminal (final) electron acceptor of the electron transport chain?
options: Oxygen
NAD
Carbon dioxide
Pyruvate
questions.explain: Oxygen is the final electron acceptor, combining with electrons and protons to form water.

questions.q: Which statement about the role of reduced NAD and reduced FAD in respiration is correct?
options: They are produced only during oxidative phosphorylation
They directly phosphorylate ADP to ATP
They are the final electron acceptors of the chain
They deliver electrons and protons to the electron transport chain
questions.explain: Reduced coenzymes carry electrons and protons to the carriers on the inner membrane, feeding the chain.

questions.q: Enzymes increase the rate of reaction by:
options: raising the temperature of the substrate
increasing the activation energy of the reaction
lowering the activation energy by providing an alternative reaction pathway
being permanently changed by the reaction
questions.explain: Enzymes lower the activation energy required, allowing more substrate molecules to react at a given temperature.

questions.q: Which is the correct order of stages in aerobic respiration?
options: Krebs cycle then glycolysis then oxidative phosphorylation then link reaction
Link reaction then glycolysis then Krebs cycle then oxidative phosphorylation
Glycolysis then Krebs cycle then link reaction then oxidative phosphorylation
Glycolysis then link reaction then Krebs cycle then oxidative phosphorylation
questions.explain: Glucose is split in glycolysis, pyruvate enters the link reaction, then the Krebs cycle, then oxidative phosphorylation.
